chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Naysaburi, from Ibrahim ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Saeed al-Makki, from Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Mazini, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits the grave of my son Ali, there is for him with Allah the reward of seventy accepted Hajjs. I said, 'Seventy Hajjs?' He said, 'Yes, and seventy thousand Hajjs.' I said, 'Seventy thousand Hajjs?' He said, 'Perhaps a Hajj is not accepted. But whoever visits him and spends the night at his side is like the one who visited Allah at His Throne.'

He said, 'Yes. When it is the Day of Judgment, there will be upon the Throne of the Beneficent four from the former [prophets] and four from the later ones. As for the four who are from the former, they are Noah, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (peace be upon them). And as for the four from the later ones, they are Muhammad, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). Then the area will be extended, and those who visited the graves of the Imams (peace be upon them) will sit with us, except that the one with the highest rank and the closest in receiving gifts will be the visitors of the grave of my son Ali (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Ali al-Reza (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the superior merit of visiting Imam Ali al-Reza (as), equating it to seventy thousand accepted Hajjs, while distinguishing true acceptance from mere ritual. It places this ziyarah within a grand eschatological framework where the Prophet, the Imams, and previous prophets sit on the Throne, with visitors of the Imams' graves granted the highest rank and closest proximity to the Divine Presence.
